Solution: An infinite limit describes outputs exceeding every bound in a specified direction; infinity is not a finite real value. Question Choices: At what x-value does f(x) = 1/(x - 6) have a vertical asymptote?
Hints: Set the denominator to zero.|Solve x - 6 = 0.
Solution: For a rational function, record all original denominator zeros. Reduce completely. If every denominator factor vanishing at an excluded input disappears, the reduced expression has a finite value there and the exclusion is a removable hole. If a vanishing denominator factor remains after full reduction, the point is a pole and gives a vertical asymptote. The vertical asymptote is x = 6.
